Change c0075. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. II; 1831 Ch. III.

Context before (unchanged): His manners in private were even more mild and attractive than in public; for there was a certain dignity in his mien during his lecture, which in his own house was replaced by the greatest affability and kindness.

1818 text: He heard with attention my little narration concerning my studies, and smiled at the names of Cornelius Agrippa, and Paracelsus, but without the contempt that M. Krempe had exhibited.

1831 text: I gave him pretty nearly the same account of my former pursuits as I had given to his fellow-professor. He heard with attention the little narration concerning my studies, and smiled at the names of Cornelius Agrippa and Paracelsus, but without the contempt that M. Krempe had exhibited.

Context after (unchanged): He said, that "these were men to whose indefatigable zeal modern philosophers were indebted for most of the foundations of their knowledge.

result.rationale: Adds a new sentence linking Clerval-like account to Krempe ('same account... as I had given to his fellow-professor'), a elaboration of the scene; other edits ('my' to 'the', comma deletion) are minor wording and punctuation.
